prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Spindrift (company_id spindrift; category: sparkling water and soda made with real fruit)
Official domains: drinkspindrift.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://drinkspindrift.com/pages/about-us | document: official_domain | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Half & Half hit shelves and brought real brewed tea to our lineup. We launched a direct-to-consumer experience to bring the full real fruit lineup to the masses. With real squeezed fruit, no added sugar. We launched Spindrift® Spiked, a hard seltzer made our way. For people who appreciate real ingredients, incredible taste, with a little ABV. We brought back Blackberry."

"“I Wasn't a Fan of Hard Seltzer, but Spindrift's New Spiked Seltzers Completely Changed My Mind\" Bill Creelman featured on \"How I Built This\" podcast “Is The Soda Pop Market Dying? "Many e-commerce brands have requested feedback from their followers while brainstorming new styles and colors. As Spindrift builds out its portfolio of products, Shum said the company wants to grow its army of fans through new channels such as TikTok, which Spindrift launched in April."

"“Unlike flavored seltzers that have just a twinge of lime or lemon flavor, the juice adds color and a touch of natural sweetness that puts Spindrift a step above the rest.\" “A new class of social media managers is adopting a vernacular that diverges from the mother tongue of advertising.” \"The all-around, unanimous crowd favorite won us over with its natural fruit flavors and un-cloying sweetness\" “Spindrift is the crème de la crème thanks to its delicious range of flavors and lack of artificial ingredients\" “Spiked line is “better-for-you” because it is made with real fruit and has color."

[P5] source: https://www.modernretail.co/marketing/how-sparkling-water-brand-spindrift-harnesses-its-spinfluencers-to-generate-buzz/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2020 | published: unknown
"They’re also known to search for hard-to-find Spindrift flavors, with some driving hours to find cans not available in their state. While the Spinfluencer program is still small, obsessive fans like these have helped Spindrift grow to $100 million in sales as of 2020. The strategy is part of the company’s approach to community-building, and it attributes these fan-geared campaigns for the following it has cultivated among sparkling water drinkers."

[P6] source: https://www.modernretail.co/marketing/how-sparkling-water-brand-spindrift-harnesses-its-spinfluencers-to-generate-buzz/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2010, 2018 | published: unknown
"Melissa Shum, senior director of consumer marketing at Spindrift, told Modern Retail “our community is our North Star — we call them ‘the drifters,’ and they’re the biggest fans of the brands who tell everyone about it.” Spindrift, founded in 2010 in Charlestown, Mass., was largely known as a regional seltzer startup for the first few years of operation. It wasn’t until 2018 that the company started to get national distribution through retailers like Whole Foods and Target, which helped it better compete with major players like La Croix."

[P7] source: https://drinkspindrift.com/pages/press | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Non-carbonated, slightly sweet & totally crisp. New Spindrift® Tea! Crisp, non-carbonated, & slightly sweet. CHECK OUT OUR COLLAB WITH DAK PRESCOTT! CHECK OUT OUR COLLAB WITH DAK PRESCOTT! ← →"

[P8] source: https://drinkspindrift.com/pages/about-us | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2021 | published: unknown
"We had to sunset the flavor in 2021, after a heat wave in the Pacific Northwest devastated the nation’s blackberry supply, resulting in lower quality yield of fruit and steep pricing. After 3 years of hard work, our team finally found a way to bring the flavor back as a limited release batch for fans."

[P9] source: https://www.adaminsights.com/how-to-design-product-packaging-that-clearly-communicates-your-core-mission-lessons-from-spindrifts-300m-success/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: October 26, 2024 | published: unknown
"Final Thought: It’s a $300 Million Question Just like Spindrift’s redesign unlocked massive growth, a clear focus on your core mission in product packaging can propel your brand to new heights. [P10] source: https://www.themany.com/projects/yup-thats-it | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Real Good Casting. Real Good Design. We crafted a campaign that mirrored Spindrift's simplicity and honesty, focusing on the \"Just sparkling water & real squeezed fruit. Yup, that’s it\" narrative. Leveraging the charm and appeal of Kristen Bell, a beloved fan and embodiment of Spindrift's values, we created a series of engaging videos and social media content. This approach was complemented by art direction inspired by the product's design, ensuring instant shelf recognition and brand recall. The Many The Many The Many"
